rationale: Nothing is on file. MSI-H is genuinely rare in sarcoma, 0.7 percent in the largest clinically sequenced series and under 0.3 percent in an earlier 7,494-tumor cohort, concentrated in pleomorphic and radiation-associated subtypes, so a stable result is the expected one. The four stains are cheap, come back in days on the existing block, and a positive result would put approved checkpoint blockade in front of a patient who otherwise has no approved targeted option, along with a Lynch syndrome question for her and her relatives.
notes: A dMMR call would reflex to MLH1 promoter methylation testing and to germline evaluation.

rationale: Untested. In the reference series PD-L1 was positive in 9 of 22 and then 11 of 21 dedifferentiated chondrosarcomas across two cohorts, and in none of 119 conventional, 19 mesenchymal or 20 clear cell tumors, with staining confined to the dedifferentiated component and tracking with tumor-infiltrating lymphocytes; a second group reported PD-L1 in a third of dedifferentiated tumors with CD8 T cells present in 90 percent of them. A positive result does not unlock an approved drug, since no sarcoma indication is keyed to PD-L1, so treat it as trial-enrichment information and make sure the section stained actually contains dedifferentiated tissue, or the result will be falsely negative.
notes: Clone and scoring system must be recorded, because a result generated with one companion diagnostic does not transfer to another protocol's cutoff.

rationale: No expression data exists. Nothing behind this target is approved, so a positive stain buys trial candidacy rather than a prescription, and sponsors generally re-test centrally with their own antibody, which makes a local stain a triage tool rather than an eligibility document.
notes: Most B7-H3 trials require ECOG 0-1. The ECOG of 2 in the profile was assumed at intake rather than measured, so it may be what closes this route, or may not apply at all once someone scores it.
